source.title: On open problems based on fuzzy filters of pseudo BCK-algebras

accepted.question_text: Let A be a pseudo-BCK algebra with binary operations customarily written as ⇀ and ⇝, order relation inherited from those operations, and top element 1. In the bounded case, assume A also has a least element 0 in the sense used for bounded pseudo-BCK algebras. A nonempty subset F of A is a pseudo-filter when it is upward closed and closed under the pseudo-BCK filter rule: if x is in F and either x ⇀ y or x ⇝ y is in F, then y is in F. Such a pseudo-filter F is called implicative when, for every x and y in A, membership of (x ⇀ y) ⇀ x in F forces x to be in F and membership of (x ⇝ y) ⇝ x in F forces x to be in F. It is called Boolean when, for every x and y in A, membership of (x ⇀ y) ⇝ x in F forces x to be in F and membership of (x ⇝ y) ⇀ x in F forces x to be in F. In pseudo-BCK algebras, and separately in bounded pseudo-BCK algebras, are the notions of implicative pseudo-filter and Boolean filter equivalent?
accepted.context_brief: Equivalence of implicative and Boolean pseudo-filters

evidence.quote: Is the notion of implicative pseudo-filter equivalent to the notion of Boolean filter?

accepted.question_text: Let A be a pseudo-BCK algebra with binary operations ⇀ and ⇝ and top element 1. Call A an implicative pseudo-BCK algebra when, for every x and y in A, the identities (x ⇝ y) ⇀ x = x and (x ⇀ y) ⇝ x = x hold. A nonempty subset F of A is a pseudo-filter when it is upward closed and satisfies the closure rule that x in F together with either x ⇀ y in F or x ⇝ y in F implies y in F. A pseudo-filter F is Boolean when (x ⇀ y) ⇝ x in F implies x in F and (x ⇝ y) ⇀ x in F implies x in F for all x,y; it is implicative when (x ⇀ y) ⇀ x in F implies x in F and (x ⇝ y) ⇝ x in F implies x in F for all x,y. Prove or disprove the proposed characterization that A is an implicative pseudo-BCK algebra if and only if every pseudo-filter of A is a Boolean filter, equivalently if and only if every pseudo-filter of A is an implicative pseudo-filter.
accepted.context_brief: Characterizing implicative pseudo-BCK algebras by pseudo-filters

evidence.quote: Prove or negate the following conclusion
A pseudo-BCK algebra is an implicative pseudo-BCK algebra

trace.notes: Normalized the input as one zbMATH resolver URL with trailing identifier 6720277.
Direct shell fetch of the zbMATH resolver returned a Cloudflare 403 challenge. Local shard metadata identified the exact work title, publication year, and DOI 10.3233/IFS-151938.

The DOI resolved to the SAGE-hosted article page for the same title. Direct shell requests to the publisher HTML, PDF, and legacy IOS Press endpoints were blocked by Cloudflare; exact-title search recovered readable article-body text for the same DOI and title, so that article body was used as the HTML primary source.

Mapped the HTML article body: Abstract names two open problems and states they are partly solved; Section 1 introduces the two problems and motivation; Section 2 gives pseudo-BCK and bounded pseudo-BCK preliminaries, including the 2-type implicative pseudo-BCK definition; Section 3 defines pseudo-filter, implicative pseudo-filter, Boolean filter, and fuzzy variants; Section 4 states results toward the two open problems; Section 5 summarizes that the article proposes solutions and leaves broader common pseudo-BCK cases for future work.

Section 4 restates the two open problems and supplies partial theorems for bounded pseudo-BCK algebras and pseudo-BCK algebras with product operation; these restatements were treated as duplicate evidence rather than additional questions.
